description: The hydrography layers of the U.S. Census Bureau's TIGER/Line Shapefiles are extracts from the MAF/TIGER database that describe surface water as the Census Bureau maps it for its statistical geography. Area Hydrography (county files) contains perennial and intermittent water polygons: ponds, lakes, oceans, swamps, glaciers and the area of large double-line rivers. Linear Hydrography (county files) contains all linear features with hydrography codes: streams and rivers, braided streams, canals, ditches, artificial paths and aqueducts. A national Coastline file and shoreline edges in the All Lines layer complete the set, and relationship files link water polygons to topological faces. Coverage: the 50 states, the District of Columbia, Puerto Rico and the Island Areas; annual vintages, the 2025 files released on 23 September 2025 with feature updates through July 2025. Format and access: shapefiles by county on the Census Bureau's FTP site and web interface, plus national and state geodatabases and GeoPackages; free and public domain. Caveats: the features are drawn for census mapping, not hydrology; artificial paths may not match the USGS National Hydrography Dataset and do not carry NHD codes, and there is no flow direction or network attribute. Simulation uses: a nationally consistent water layer tied to census blocks, useful for masking water from exposure grids, linking canals and aqueducts to water-supply models, and locating riverine and coastal assets relative to population. Related records: TIGER/Line road and rail layers, the TIGER edges and faces topology, TIGER boundaries and blocks, and TIGERweb, which serves the same layers as map services.
